items.prompt: They say grandpa used to get up early every morning.
items.explanation: “Every morning” is a habit: -ar. “They say” is hearsay: -mış. Together: kalkarmış — no extra words needed.
It ends in -ız. That’s “we”: yapar-mış-ız. Turkish doesn’t need “we” in front.

items.prompt: Bu fırın çok güzel boyoz yaparmış. Has the speaker tried it?
options: No, they heard it from others
items.say: Bu fırın çok güzel boyoz yaparmış.
items.explanation: -mış means someone told them. They haven’t eaten this boyoz themselves.
gel is on the list of thirteen: gelir. The vowel i carries over into miş.

items.prompt: How does a Turkish fairy tale begin?
items.explanation: Nobody saw the fairy tale. So it’s -mış from the very first line — like “once upon a time,” but built into the verb.

exercises.instruction: Match the form with the meaning

pairs.right: they say he used to get up (usually)

items.explanation: -tı — saw it yourself (simple past). -mış — heard it. -ar — a habit (simple present). -armış — a habit you heard about (“apparently used to”).

items.translation: They say grandpa used to come to Izmir every summer.
items.explanation: “Used to” is not plain -miş. gel is an exception: gelir. Plus hearsay: gelirmiş.
In English “never” is enough. In Turkish, hiç asks for a negative verb: iç-mez-miş, not içermiş.
gel is one of the thirteen exceptions: gelir, not geler.

items.translation: They say I used to cry a lot.
items.explanation: ağla ends in a vowel: just -r. Then -mış and “I” at the end: -ım. No ben needed.

items.translation: I hear you’re a great cook!
items.explanation: yap is one syllable: -ar. Hearsay: -mış. “You”: -sın.

exercises.instruction: Coordinates: put the sentence in the right quadrant
exercises.description: A sentence appears on a card, the learner picks a quadrant of the plane: saw/heard × once/usually. Logic lives in index.html.

items.explanation: -ar is a habit, -mış is hearsay. Top right quadrant.
-tı — I saw it, once.
-mış without -ar — heard about a one-time thing.
-ar without -mış — a habit I know firsthand.
“Every day” plus -mış: a habit you know from others.
dün and -di: once, and I know it for sure.

items.prompt: They say our neighbor used to play the piano every day.
items.explanation: Every day is a habit: -ar. They say is hearsay: -mış.

items.statement: okurmuş is written as one word, but okur muymuş has a space.
items.explanation: Only the question particle mI is written separately. Everything else is glued on.

items.translation: They say cats sleep sixteen hours a day.
items.explanation: uyu ends in a vowel: -r. The vowel u carries over into muş.
English “never” keeps the verb positive. Turkish doesn’t: the negative of a habit is -mez. Harmony: söyle → -mez → -miş.

items.prompt: They say we used to go to Çeşme every summer. Biz her yaz Çeşme'ye ___.
items.explanation: git gets voiced before a vowel: gider. “We” is -iz.
